name: Pain during sex
summary: Pain during or after sex is common and has many causes, including vaginal dryness, infections and endometriosis. It is worth seeing a doctor, as most causes can be treated.
redFlags: Sudden severe tummy or pelvic pain after sex, especially if you could be pregnant
Severe pain with fainting, dizziness or heavy bleeding
urgentFlags: Pain with a high temperature or unusual discharge
Bleeding after sex with pelvic pain
Painful sores or blisters on the genitals

commonCauses.title: Vaginal dryness
commonCauses.detail: Common around the menopause, after childbirth, when breastfeeding, or with not enough arousal.

commonCauses.title: Infections
commonCauses.detail: Thrush or sexually transmitted infections such as chlamydia, gonorrhoea or herpes.

commonCauses.title: Endometriosis or pelvic inflammatory disease
commonCauses.detail: Usually causes deep pain felt inside the pelvis.

commonCauses.title: Vaginismus
commonCauses.detail: The vaginal muscles tighten involuntarily, making penetration painful or impossible.

commonCauses.title: Penile conditions
commonCauses.detail: In men, a tight foreskin, infection or prostate problems can cause pain.

selfCare: Use a water-based lubricant
Take more time for arousal and try positions that allow you to control depth
Stop if it hurts and talk to your partner
Use condoms to reduce the risk of infections
avoid: Continuing sex through pain
Using oil-based lubricants with latex condoms, as they can damage them
Perfumed products in the genital area
seeDoctorIf: You keep having pain during or after sex
You have bleeding after sex
You might have a sexually transmitted infection
Pain is affecting your relationship or wellbeing

name: Testicle pain
summary: Sudden, severe testicle pain can be testicular torsion, an emergency that needs surgery within hours. Milder pain is often due to an infection or injury.
redFlags: Sudden, severe pain in one testicle
Testicle pain with feeling sick or being sick
A testicle that is higher than usual or lying at an unusual angle
Severe pain after an injury to the testicles that does not ease within an hour
Severe pain, swelling and redness of the scrotum or groin with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: Pain and swelling that came on over a day or two
Testicle pain with a high temperature
Testicle pain with burning when peeing or discharge from the penis
Pain with swelling of the scrotum

commonCauses.title: Testicular torsion
commonCauses.detail: The testicle twists and cuts off its blood supply; most common in boys and young men, and needs emergency surgery.

commonCauses.title: Epididymitis or orchitis
commonCauses.detail: Infection or inflammation causing pain and swelling, sometimes linked to sexually transmitted infections or mumps.

commonCauses.title: Injury
commonCauses.detail: A blow to the testicles; pain should ease within an hour.

commonCauses.title: Varicocele or cyst
commonCauses.detail: Swollen veins or fluid-filled lumps can cause a dull ache.

commonCauses.title: Hernia or kidney stone
commonCauses.detail: Pain can spread to the testicles from the groin or kidneys.

selfCare: Get emergency help straight away for sudden severe pain
For mild pain, wear supportive underwear and rest
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Use a cold pack wrapped in a towel for swelling after an injury
avoid: Waiting to see if sudden severe testicle pain goes away; torsion can damage the testicle within hours
Sex until an infection has been treated
seeDoctorIf: You have a dull ache in the testicles that keeps coming back
You notice a lump or change in the shape or feel of a testicle
Your scrotum feels heavy or swollen

name: Lump or swelling in a testicle
summary: Most testicle lumps are harmless, such as cysts or swollen veins, but any new lump should be checked by a doctor because testicular cancer is easier to treat when found early.
redFlags: Sudden, severe testicle pain, especially with feeling or being sick
urgentFlags: A swollen, painful testicle with a high temperature
Swelling that gets bigger quickly

commonCauses.title: Epididymal cyst
commonCauses.detail: A smooth, fluid-filled lump above or behind the testicle; usually harmless.

commonCauses.title: Varicocele
commonCauses.detail: Swollen veins that feel like a 'bag of worms', more often on the left.

commonCauses.title: Hydrocele
commonCauses.detail: Fluid around the testicle causing painless swelling.

commonCauses.title: Infection
commonCauses.detail: Epididymitis or orchitis causes painful swelling.

commonCauses.title: Testicular cancer
commonCauses.detail: Usually a painless lump or hardening; most common in men aged 15 to 49.

selfCare: Check your testicles regularly, ideally after a warm bath or shower, so you know what is normal for you
Make an appointment even if the lump is painless
avoid: Waiting to see if a lump goes away
Squeezing or pressing hard on a lump
seeDoctorIf: You notice any new lump or swelling
A testicle has changed shape, size or feels harder
You have a heavy feeling in your scrotum

name: Erection problems
summary: Difficulty getting or keeping an erection is very common and can be linked to stress, tiredness, alcohol, or health conditions such as heart disease and diabetes. It is worth seeing a doctor, as treatments work well.
redFlags: An erection lasting more than 4 hours, or a painful erection not caused by sexual arousal
Erection problems with chest pain, breathlessness or pain spreading to the arm or jaw
urgentFlags: Sudden erection problems with new numbness around the genitals, bottom or legs
A painful bend in the penis that appeared suddenly or after an injury

commonCauses.title: Stress, anxiety or relationship issues
commonCauses.detail: Often the cause when erections still happen at other times, such as in the morning.

commonCauses.title: Alcohol, smoking and tiredness
commonCauses.detail: These commonly affect erections.

commonCauses.title: Blood vessel and heart conditions
commonCauses.detail: High blood pressure, high cholesterol and heart disease reduce blood flow to the penis.

commonCauses.title: Diabetes and hormone problems
commonCauses.detail: Diabetes can affect nerves and blood vessels; low testosterone is less common.

commonCauses.title: Medicines
commonCauses.detail: Some blood pressure medicines and antidepressants can cause erection problems.

selfCare: Cut down on alcohol and stop smoking
Be more active and aim for a healthy weight
Find ways to manage stress and talk openly with your partner
Do not stop a prescribed medicine without talking to your doctor
avoid: Erection pills bought online from unregulated sellers, which may be fake or unsafe
Recreational drugs, which can make erection problems worse
seeDoctorIf: Erection problems keep happening for more than a few weeks
You also have symptoms such as feeling thirsty, peeing a lot or tiredness
You think a medicine might be causing it
It is affecting your wellbeing or relationship

name: Discharge from the penis
summary: Discharge from the penis that is not urine or semen is often caused by a sexually transmitted infection. A sexual health clinic or doctor can test and treat it.
redFlags: Being unable to pee at all
Severe pain, swelling and redness of the genitals or groin with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: Discharge with testicle pain or swelling
Discharge with a high temperature
Discharge with joint pain or a rash

commonCauses.title: Chlamydia or gonorrhoea
commonCauses.detail: Common sexually transmitted infections that often cause discharge and burning when peeing.

commonCauses.title: Non-gonococcal urethritis
commonCauses.detail: Inflammation of the tube that carries urine, often caused by an infection.

commonCauses.title: Balanitis or thrush
commonCauses.detail: Inflammation under the foreskin with a thick discharge, redness and soreness.

commonCauses.title: Trichomoniasis
commonCauses.detail: A sexually transmitted infection that can cause thin white discharge.

selfCare: Get tested at a sexual health clinic or by a doctor
Avoid sex until you and your partner have been tested and treated
Wash under the foreskin gently with water each day
avoid: Taking leftover or online antibiotics without a diagnosis
Having sex, including oral sex, until treatment is finished
seeDoctorIf: You have any unusual discharge from your penis
A partner has been diagnosed with a sexually transmitted infection
Symptoms come back after treatment

name: Sores, blisters or warts on the genitals
summary: Sores, blisters or lumps on the genitals are often caused by sexually transmitted infections such as herpes or genital warts. A sexual health clinic can diagnose and treat them.
redFlags: Rapidly spreading redness, swelling and severe pain in the genital area with a high temperature and feeling very unwell
urgentFlags: Painful sores that make it hard or impossible to pee
Sores with a high temperature, headache and feeling unwell
Genital sores during pregnancy, especially late pregnancy

commonCauses.title: Genital herpes
commonCauses.detail: Small painful blisters that burst to leave red, open sores; can come back.

commonCauses.title: Genital warts
commonCauses.detail: Painless small growths or lumps caused by HPV.

commonCauses.title: Syphilis
commonCauses.detail: A usually painless sore that heals on its own, but the infection remains and needs treatment.

commonCauses.title: Skin causes
commonCauses.detail: Ingrown hairs, spots, cysts or friction can also cause bumps.

selfCare: Get checked at a sexual health clinic
Keep the area clean and dry
Use paracetamol for pain, following the pack instructions
Bathing in salt water or applying petroleum jelly can ease herpes pain
avoid: Sex, including oral sex, until you have been checked or the sores have healed
Over-the-counter wart treatments meant for hands or feet on the genitals
Touching or picking the sores
seeDoctorIf: You have any new sore, blister or lump on the genitals
A partner has been diagnosed with a sexually transmitted infection
Sores keep coming back

name: Breast lump or change
summary: Most breast lumps are not cancer, but any new lump or change in the breast, nipple or armpit should be checked by a doctor. This applies to men too.
redFlags: A red, hot, painful breast with a high temperature and feeling very unwell, confused or faint
urgentFlags: A red, hot, swollen and painful area of the breast, especially when breastfeeding
A painful lump with a high temperature

commonCauses.title: Cysts
commonCauses.detail: Fluid-filled sacs that can feel smooth and may be tender, often around periods.

commonCauses.title: Fibroadenoma
commonCauses.detail: A smooth, rubbery, movable lump, common in younger women.

commonCauses.title: Mastitis or abscess
commonCauses.detail: Painful, hot, red breast, usually when breastfeeding.

commonCauses.title: Breast cancer
commonCauses.detail: Can cause a lump, skin dimpling, a nipple change or discharge, or a lump in the armpit.

selfCare: Get to know how your breasts normally look and feel
Book an appointment for any new lump or change, even if painless
Attend breast screening when invited
avoid: Waiting until after your next period to see if a lump goes away if you are worried
Assuming a painless lump is harmless
seeDoctorIf: You find a new lump or thickening in the breast or armpit
Your breast changes size or shape, or the skin dimples or puckers
You have nipple discharge, a rash on the nipple or a nipple that turns inwards
You are a man with a breast lump

name: Breast pain
summary: Breast pain is common, often linked to periods, pregnancy or a poorly fitting bra, and is rarely a sign of cancer on its own.
redFlags: Chest pain that spreads to the arm, neck, jaw or back, or comes with breathlessness or sweating
A red, hot, painful breast with feeling very unwell, confused or faint
urgentFlags: A red, hot, swollen area of the breast, especially when breastfeeding
Breast pain with a high temperature

commonCauses.title: Hormonal changes
commonCauses.detail: Pain in both breasts in the days before a period, during pregnancy or when starting hormonal medicines.

commonCauses.title: Bra fit or exercise
commonCauses.detail: A poorly fitting bra or lack of support during activity.

commonCauses.title: Breastfeeding problems
commonCauses.detail: Blocked ducts, mastitis or sore nipples.

commonCauses.title: Chest wall pain
commonCauses.detail: Muscle strain or inflammation of the rib joints can feel like breast pain.

selfCare: Wear a well-fitting, supportive bra, including a sports bra for exercise and a soft bra at night
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen, following the pack instructions
Keep a diary to see if pain is linked to your periods
If breastfeeding, keep feeding or expressing and ask a midwife or health visitor about positioning
avoid: Stopping breastfeeding suddenly if you have a blocked duct or mastitis
Supplements such as evening primrose oil, which have little evidence of benefit
seeDoctorIf: Pain is not linked to your periods and has lasted more than a few weeks
Pain is in one specific area
You also have a lump, nipple discharge or skin changes
Pain is affecting your daily life

name: Hot flushes
summary: Hot flushes are sudden feelings of heat in the face, neck and chest, very common around the menopause. Lifestyle changes and treatments from a doctor can help.
redFlags: Flushing with swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, wheezing or difficulty breathing
urgentFlags: Night sweats with a high temperature or unexplained weight loss
Flushing with a racing heartbeat, tremor and weight loss

commonCauses.title: Menopause and perimenopause
commonCauses.detail: The most common cause, due to falling oestrogen levels, usually from the mid-40s.

commonCauses.title: Medicines
commonCauses.detail: Some cancer treatments and other medicines cause flushes.

commonCauses.title: Overactive thyroid
commonCauses.detail: Feeling hot, sweating, a fast heartbeat and weight loss.

commonCauses.title: Triggers
commonCauses.detail: Alcohol, caffeine, spicy food and stress can bring on flushes.

selfCare: Wear light layers and keep your bedroom cool
Cut down on alcohol, caffeine and spicy food
Exercise regularly and stop smoking
Cognitive behavioural therapy has evidence for reducing the impact of hot flushes
avoid: Unregulated herbal remedies, which may be unproven or interact with other medicines
'Bioidentical' hormones from unregulated sources
seeDoctorIf: Hot flushes or other menopause symptoms are affecting your life
You have symptoms under the age of 45
You want to discuss treatments such as hormone replacement therapy

name: Sickness in pregnancy
summary: Feeling sick and vomiting are common in early pregnancy and usually improve by weeks 16 to 20. Severe vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down needs treatment.
redFlags: Vomiting blood
Severe tummy pain, or one-sided pain with shoulder-tip pain or fainting
Confusion, fainting or extreme drowsiness
urgentFlags: Being unable to keep any food or fluids down for 24 hours
Very dark pee or not peeing for more than 8 hours
Feeling dizzy or weak when standing
Vomiting with a high temperature or pain when peeing
Losing weight

commonCauses.title: Normal pregnancy sickness
commonCauses.detail: Linked to pregnancy hormones; can happen at any time of day.

commonCauses.title: Hyperemesis gravidarum
commonCauses.detail: Severe, persistent sickness that can cause dehydration and needs medical treatment.

commonCauses.title: Other illness
commonCauses.detail: Stomach bugs or urine infections can cause vomiting during pregnancy too.

selfCare: Rest when you can, as tiredness can make sickness worse
Eat small, frequent meals of plain foods high in carbohydrate
Sip drinks little and often rather than large amounts
Foods or drinks containing ginger may help
Ask your midwife, doctor or pharmacist before taking any medicine
avoid: Foods or smells that make you feel sick
Taking over-the-counter sickness medicines without checking they are safe in pregnancy
Going long periods without eating or drinking
seeDoctorIf: Sickness is affecting your daily life
Self-care measures are not helping
Sickness continues beyond 20 weeks or starts later in pregnancy

name: Bleeding or pain in early pregnancy
summary: Light bleeding in early pregnancy is fairly common and does not always mean a problem, but it should always be checked, as it can be a sign of miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy.
redFlags: Sharp, sudden or severe pain in your tummy, especially on one side
Pain in the tip of your shoulder
Dizziness, fainting or feeling very unwell
Heavy bleeding, soaking through pads, or passing large clots
Pain when pooing or peeing with bleeding and feeling faint
urgentFlags: Any vaginal bleeding during pregnancy
Cramping pain in the lower tummy
Bleeding or pain after a positive pregnancy test when you have not yet had a scan
A gush of fluid from the vagina

commonCauses.title: Implantation bleeding or cervical changes
commonCauses.detail: Light spotting can happen early in pregnancy or after sex because the cervix is more sensitive.

commonCauses.title: Miscarriage
commonCauses.detail: Bleeding with cramping in the first 23 weeks; sadly common, especially in the first 12 weeks.

commonCauses.title: Ectopic pregnancy
commonCauses.detail: The pregnancy grows outside the womb, usually in a tube; it can cause one-sided pain, bleeding and shoulder-tip pain and is an emergency.

commonCauses.title: Infection
commonCauses.detail: Vaginal or cervical infections can cause light bleeding.

selfCare: Contact your midwife, doctor or an early pregnancy unit the same day
Use pads rather than tampons so the amount of bleeding can be judged
Rest while you wait to be seen
avoid: Waiting at home with severe pain or heavy bleeding
Using tampons while bleeding in pregnancy
Taking anti-inflammatory painkillers such as ibuprofen in pregnancy unless advised
seeDoctorIf: You had bleeding that has stopped but you have not yet been checked
You have had a previous ectopic pregnancy or miscarriage and are pregnant again
